context.analysis:
## Overview
[System Overview]
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS while routing suspicious cases to analysts.
- Core purpose is providing sub-50ms fraud decisions and case management while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
- External Payment Gateway
- API Gateway / ALB (Edge with Circuit Breaker)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate containers)
- Case Management UI (Fraud Analyst interface)
- Amazon SQS / Amazon Kinesis (Asynchronous event bus)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock / Amazon QLDB (Tamper-evident audit storage)
- AWS KMS (Key Management Service)
- GitHub Actions (CI/CD deployment pipeline)

## Relationships
- External Payment Gateway to API Gateway/ALB via HTTPS / mTLS
- API Gateway/ALB to Fraud Scoring Engine via HTTP/2 and gRPC
- Fraud Scoring Engine to Amazon SQS/Kinesis via AWS SDK (TLS 1.3)
- Amazon SQS/Kinesis to S3 Object Lock / QLDB for asynchronous audit logs
- Fraud Analysts to Case Management UI via HTTPS (OAuth2/OIDC, WebAuthn MFA)
- GitHub Actions to AWS ECS Fargate via AWS API for zero-downtime blue/green deployments

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration to avoid memory-heavy ML overhead and cap idle infrastructure costs within budget.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock / QLDB: Tamper-evident storage implementing cryptographic hash chaining (Merkle trees) for 7-year auditability.
- AWS KMS: Envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) for data protection and strict separation of card and audit keys.
- AWS API Gateway / ALB: Edge routing providing circuit-breaker capabilities for high availability and fail-open handling.
- GitHub Actions & AWS Signer: Automated blue/green deployment pipelines with cryptographic container image and model verification.

## Rationale
- This architecture prioritizes managed AWS services to fit within a strict €25,000 monthly budget and a 3-person engineering team. 
- Asynchronous logging and lightweight containerization decouple high-throughput scoring from compliance requirements, guaranteeing sub-50ms latency and PCI-DSS Level 1 security.

## Overview
[Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst reviews. Core purpose is ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliant, low-latency fraud decisions within budget.]

## Key Elements
- External Payment Gateway
- Fraud Analyst, Risk Operations Manager, Fraud Data Scientist
- API Gateway / Ingress Container
- Scoring Engine Container
- Case Management Container
- AWS SageMaker Serverless Inference
- Amazon Aurora Serverless / QLDB / S3 Object Lock
- AWS ECR, AWS Inspector, AWS Signer
- AWS Secrets Manager, AWS CloudWatch, AWS X-Ray

## Relationships
- External Payment Gateway interacts with API Gateway via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- API Gateway routes scoring requests to Scoring Engine Container via REST over internal VPC
- Scoring Engine invokes AWS SageMaker Serverless Inference via AWS SDK
- Scoring Engine writes tamper-evident decision logs to QLDB / S3 with Object Lock
- Fraud Analysts access Case Management Container via HTTPS with OIDC/OAuth2 MFA
- Case Management reads and writes review cases in Aurora Serverless

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration chosen to minimize operational toil for a 3-engineer team
- AWS SageMaker Serverless Inference: Decouples model updates for zero-downtime scoring (R-03)
- Amazon S3 Object Lock & QLDB: Tamper-evident storage for 7-year audit retention (R-06)
- AWS Secrets Manager: Automatic rotation of database credentials and API keys
- AWS CloudWatch & X-Ray: Distributed tracing and metric alarms for <50ms P99 latency tracking (R-04)
- Native VPC Security Groups & IAM: Container isolation without App Mesh complexity

## Rationale
[This architecture leverages fully managed AWS services to fit the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and operational capacity of a three-engineer team. It ensures PCI-DSS compliance, tamper-evident 7-year auditability, and sub-50ms P99 latency while maintaining high availability and fail-safe controls.]

Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance constraints. It provides real-time scoring within 50ms and case management capabilities for fraud analysts in AWS region eu-west-1.

## Key Elements
- **Fraud Analyst**: Primary business user reviewing suspicious transactions.
- **API Gateway / Ingress Container**: AWS ECS Fargate container handling incoming HTTP REST traffic.
- **Scoring Engine Container**: AWS ECS Fargate container executing fraud scoring logic.
- **SageMaker Real-Time Endpoint**: Isolated AWS SageMaker model inference backend in a private subnet.
- **Amazon SQS & DLQ**: Asynchronous message queue with Dead-Letter Queue for audit logging.
- **Amazon QLDB / Amazon S3 Object Lock**: Tamper-evident storage for 7-year audit compliance.
- **GitHub Actions**: CI/CD pipeline automating blue/green zero-downtime deployments.

## Relationships
- API Gateway / Ingress Container -> Scoring Engine Container: Routes scoring requests [REST over internal VPC using TLS 1.3/mTLS]
- Scoring Engine Container -> SageMaker Real-Time Endpoint: Invokes model inference [AWS SDK over VPC interface endpoints]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon SQS: Offloads audit logs asynchronously [AWS SDK with AWS KMS encryption]
- Amazon SQS -> Amazon QLDB / S3 Object Lock: Persists tamper-evident decision logs [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Compute platform chosen for zero-server management, fitting the 3-engineer team constraint.
- **AWS SageMaker Real-Time Endpoints**: ML hosting selected over Serverless to eliminate cold starts and meet the 50ms P99 latency SLA (R-04).
- **Amazon SQS & QLDB**: Decoupled asynchronous architecture chosen to protect decision latency while guaranteeing 7-year auditability (R-06).
- **AWS Secrets Manager**: Secure credential injection ensuring zero hardcoded secrets for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance (R-05).
- **GitHub Actions & AWS ECS**: Automation toolchain enabling zero-downtime model updates (R-03) within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Rationale
This architecture balances ultra-low latency (50ms P99) and stringent security constraints through decoupled asynchronous logging and dedicated model endpoints. It remains operable by a 3-engineer team within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget by leveraging serverless and managed AWS services.

Case Management Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Container empowers fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions and audit scoring decisions securely. It enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while supporting low-latency analyst workflows.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS Fargate Container)
- Amazon Aurora Serverless (Database Container)
- Amazon SQS (Message Queue Container)
- Amazon QLDB / S3 Object Lock (Immutable Ledger System)
- AWS Secrets Manager (Security Service)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management Container: Accesses review cases and audit trails [HTTPS with OIDC/OAuth2 MFA]
- Case Management Container -> Amazon Aurora Serverless: Reads and writes review cases and read-optimized audit projections [Database Protocol]
- Case Management Container -> Amazon SQS: Routes failed audit logs or feedback events to a Dead-Letter Queue [AWS SDK / SQS Protocol]
- Case Management Container -> Amazon QLDB / S3 Object Lock: Writes cryptographically signed analyst actions and overrides [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Case Management Container -> AWS Secrets Manager: Fetches database credentials and OIDC secrets [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Hosts containerized application with service auto-scaling for cost control within budget.
- Amazon Aurora Serverless: Stores review cases and event-driven projections for query performance.
- Amazon SQS: Handles asynchronous dead-letter queues to prevent data loss during outages.
- AWS Secrets Manager: Secures credentials and secrets with automated rotation.
- OIDC/OAuth2: Authenticates analysts and enforces strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).

## Rationale
This architecture ensures robust security and strict compliance (PCI-DSS Level 1, 7-year auditability) without compromising performance or exceeding the fixed monthly budget. Asynchronous processing and read-optimized projections protect core ledgers while maximizing analyst efficiency.

AWS SageMaker Serverless Inference.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst reviews. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 transactions per second.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (User)
- External Payment Gateway, GitHub Actions (External Systems)
- API Gateway / Ingress Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Scoring Engine Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Model Inference Runtime (AWS ECS Fargate running ONNX)
- Amazon Aurora Serverless (Amazon Aurora)
- Amazon QLDB / S3 Object Lock (Amazon QLDB / Amazon S3)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container: Forwards authorization requests [HTTPS / REST]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Model Inference Runtime: Invokes fraud scoring [gRPC / Internal Network]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon Aurora: Queries and stores transaction state [PostgreSQL Protocol / TLS 1.3]
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management Container: Reviews suspicious payments [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Case Management Container -> Amazon QLDB / S3 Object Lock: Stores tamper-evident audit logs [AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- Compute: AWS ECS Fargate for unified, serverless container orchestration within the 3-engineer operational capacity.
- ML Inference: ONNX Runtime for high-performance, low-latency model execution without cold-start penalties.
- Database: Amazon Aurora Serverless for scalable transactional data storage.
- Audit Storage: Amazon QLDB / S3 Object Lock for immutable 7-year audit logging to satisfy compliance (R-06).
- Security: AWS KMS for Customer Managed Keys and TLS 1.3 for data encryption in transit.

## Rationale
This unified AWS ECS Fargate and ONNX architecture avoids serverless cold-start latency to guarantee P99 performance under 50ms at 3,000 TPS. It minimizes operational overhead for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraint.

- Case Management Container -> Amazon S3: Archives cold case records older than 12 months [HTTPS / AWS SDK]
- Aurora Serverless -> Amazon CloudWatch: Streams advanced audit logs [CloudWatch Agent / KMS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration for microservices, chosen for low operational overhead.
- Amazon Aurora Serverless (v2): Relational database for case management, configured with auto-pause disabled and 0.5–8 ACUs.
- AWS IAM Database Authentication: Eliminates static credentials to meet PCI-DSS Level 1 security constraints.
- Terraform / CloudFormation: Infrastructure as Code for repeatable, auditable deployments.
- AWS KMS: Customer-managed keys for database storage and log encryption.

## Rationale
[This architecture balances stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 security and 7-year auditability requirements with the resource limitations of a 3-engineer team. By leveraging fully managed AWS services like Aurora Serverless, Fargate, and SageMaker, the system achieves high availability and sub-50ms latency within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]

## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform for a mid-size payment processor. Its core purpose is to evaluate card-not-present payment authorizations and manage fraud reviews.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Compliance Auditor
- External Payment Gateway & GitHub Actions
- AWS ECS Fargate Containers (API Gateway, Scoring Engine, Case Management)
- Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference
- Amazon Aurora Serverless
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock (Compliance Mode) & AWS KMS

## Relationships
- External Payment Gateway -> API Gateway: Forwards payment authorizations [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container: Routes authorization payloads [gRPC]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon SageMaker: Invokes fraud models [AWS SDK]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon S3: Writes tamper-evident decision logs [HTTPS/AWS SDK, TLS 1.3]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon Aurora Serverless: Queries rules and persists cases [PostgreSQL Protocol]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration to match the 3-engineer operational capacity limit.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode): Immutable storage guaranteeing 7-year audit retention.
- Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference: Managed machine learning scaling for sub-50ms P99 latency.
- Amazon Aurora Serverless: Relational storage for rules and case management.
- AWS KMS: Customer-managed key encryption with locked policies for data protection.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages serverless and managed AWS services in eu-west-1 to achieve PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and stringent auditability. It maintains high performance while respecting the strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget and three-engineer operational constraint.
